subject: biology
title: Movement and Support
welcome_lead: Step inside the body to meet the systems that keep you standing, moving and breathing.
meta_desc: KS3 Biology adventure on skeletal, muscular and respiratory body systems.
final_note: You now know how three key systems support, move and oxygenate your body.

concepts.def: Bones that support and protect the body.
Muscles that pull bones to make movement.
Lungs and airways that bring in oxygen.
Where two bones meet and allow movement.
Organ where oxygen enters the blood.
Sheet of muscle that helps you breathe.

walkthroughs.body_html: The skeleton gives shape, protects organs (skull, ribs), allows movement at joints and makes blood cells inside bones.
Muscles connect to bones by tendons. When a muscle contracts it pulls a bone. Muscles can only pull, never push, so they work in pairs.
Air enters your nose or mouth, travels down the trachea and into the lungs. The diaphragm moves down to draw air in and up to push it out.

mcqs.q: What does insulin do to blood glucose?
options: Insulin raises blood glucose to give the body energy.
Frameshift mutations are usually silent because cells can correct them.
It lowers blood glucose by causing cells (especially liver and muscle) to take it up and store it as glycogen.
Insulin destroys glucose in the bloodstream so it cannot be used.

mcqs.q: How does myelination increase the speed of nerve impulse conduction?
options: Frameshift mutations are usually silent because cells can correct them.
Myelin contains additional ion channels that speed up depolarisation.
Myelin makes the axon thicker so the signal travels faster through more material.
Action potentials jump between nodes of Ranvier (saltatory conduction), skipping the myelinated sections.

mcqs.q: Why are frameshift mutations usually more severe than point substitutions?
options: Frameshift mutations are usually silent because cells can correct them.
Insertions/deletions of a non-multiple of 3 shift the reading frame, changing every codon downstream of the mutation.
Frameshifts only change the codon at the site of the mutation, like a substitution.
Insulin destroys glucose in the bloodstream so it cannot be used.
